content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 696 bytes (min+gzip), 87 bytes of own code. I couldn't compare either number to the original, because lodash isn't in `node_modules` and the size script fails on `src/module.ts`.

The installed es-toolkit is 1.53.2. I read the declarations and sources for `words`, `groupBy` and the compat `isEmpty` before choosing:

| Function | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `words` | `es-toolkit/string` `words` | Same call shape as lodash. |
| `groupBy` | `es-toolkit/array` `groupBy` | The main entry has no property-name shorthand, so I pass `(row) => row.age`. This is the only adapter. |
| `isEmpty` | `es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty` (default export) | The main entry has no `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`. That doesn't treat numbers, booleans or strings the way lodash does, so I used the compat version. |

Exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged, and there are no lodash imports left.

I ran the es-toolkit functions on a few sample inputs. I didn't run the lodash originals, so I haven't confirmed the results equal lodash's.

- **`words`:** `"Id_MAX "` gives `["Id","MAX"]`, `""` gives `[]`, and `"a1B2-c_d.e9XMLHttp"` splits letters from digits and `XMLHttp` into `XML` and `Http`. That is what lodash does, from memory.
- **`isEmpty`:**
  - It returns `true` for `null`, booleans, integers (including `-5`), `""`, `[]` and `{}`.
  - It returns `false` for `"a"`, `[1]`, `{a:1}` and `{theme:[43,null,89]}`.
